chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would slaughter two rams on the Day of Sacrifice, one on behalf of himself and the other on behalf of someone from his community who could not find (afford) it; and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would slaughter two rams, one on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the other on behalf of himself.

key_terms.عَمَّنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ: On behalf of someone who could not find/afford

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali perform the Eid al-Adha sacrifice regarding vicarious atonement?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi illustrates the distinct juristic practices of the Prophet and Imam Ali regarding vicarious sacrifice (Qurbani), highlighting the Prophet's role in providing for the needy within his Ummah and Imam Ali's reciprocal devotion. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the sufficiency of individual sacrifices in Shia fiqh and underscores the spiritual hierarchy and intercessory nature of the Ahl al-Bayt. The practice reflects the broader Islamic principle of charity and the specific status of the Imams as spiritual guides who carry the burdens of the community.
